title: The ULTIMATE Biceps Exercises Tier-List (Arnold-tier to Noodle-tier)
summary: NH ranks about 30 biceps exercises into Arnold (S), Excellent (A), Decent (B), Mediocre (C) and Noodle (D) tiers based on his experience. Top picks are the EZ-bar preacher curl, spider curl, behind-the-back cable curl and close-grip EZ curl; he slams cheat barbell curls, one-arm chin-ups and waiter curls, and calls incline curls and chin-ups overrated for biceps.
claims: A good biceps exercise is judged by how much biceps you use relative to the rest of the body: stable elbow and shoulder, controllable stretch, no swinging
Barbell curl is only decent: the straight bar can cause shoulder and wrist discomfort; the EZ bar was built for curls and is excellent
The arm blaster is excellent because it teaches you to curl with the biceps by locking elbows and shoulders in place
EZ-bar preacher curl is Arnold tier: both hands on one bar stretch both biceps equally, reveal the weaker arm, and train the forearm better
Unilateral curls can reinforce arm imbalances because the stronger arm lifts more; a shared bar exposes the weak side

Incline curl is mediocre and overrated: shoulders shift to assist, the stretch is less than believed, it is risky, strength drops off a cliff between reps, and it cannot be ground out safely; at most a 3rd or 4th biceps exercise
Cable curls are excellent: constant tension through the concentric and a peak contraction at the top, unlike a barbell
Cheat barbell curls are noodle tier: just a supinated clean with hip momentum; if you want negatives, do preacher curls
He did cheat curls for 10 years, tens of thousands of reps, and still says they are not a good exercise
Ring curls are decent, good for novices with difficulty adjusted by torso angle, but hard to overload and risky for biceps tears if overextended
Pelican curls give an immense stretch and gymnasts' biceps show their potency, but they need so much skill some people cut weight to do them
Spider curls are Arnold tier: like a preacher curl with full range of motion, can be ground out, and tend to relieve tendinitis whereas incline curls cause it
Chin-ups are a back exercise, not a biceps builder; few people build big biceps from chin-ups alone and EMG data claiming otherwise is flawed
One-arm chin-ups are noodle tier for biceps: twisted body, momentum, huge skill requirement and little biceps load
Hammer curls are excellent for forearms but only decent for biceps and can cause shoulder pain
Pinwheel (cross-body) curls are excellent: they hit the brachialis, brachioradialis and upper biceps; he has done them for years
Behind-the-back cable curl is Arnold tier: a pelican curl without the skill, full stretch and contraction; do not do it with dumbbells
Arm-wrestling style curls are decent; the wrist rather than the biceps is often the limiting factor
Concentration curls are excellent: elbow braced on the leg prevents rebounding, the negative is controllable and bottom half reps are safe
Seated dumbbell curls are only decent: sitting does not stop the common upper-body cheat of swinging the shoulder and elbow
Machine curls are excellent, nearly Arnold tier, but most machines are built for one body type
Waiter curls are noodle tier: cramped position, poor squeeze and no full range; promoted only by people with no muscle or on drugs
Wall curls do not stop cheating: you can push off the wall with elbows and upper back; some elbow and shoulder travel is normal in a curl
Straight-arm work (gymnastics) is decent given gymnasts' huge biceps from the loaded stretch, but you do not need that skill to grow biceps
Crucifix curls are mediocre ego exercises that hog two cable stations; a single-arm cable curl does it better
Close-grip EZ-bar curl is the king of barbell curls (Arnold tier): many variations, easy to grind, safe
He often uses partial ranges without full extension on biceps, so he occasionally uses band or cable curls to extend the arm safely for elbow and tendon health
Band curls are mediocre for building muscle; use them for recovery or to finish a session
Occlusion (blood flow restriction) curls are mediocre: a gimmick mostly pushed by enhanced lifters; he does not use them and has huge biceps
Drag curls are decent but boring and uncomfortable
Two-arm simultaneous dumbbell curls invite hip swinging and perpetuate imbalances; one arm at a time is better
High cable curls are excellent for the outer biceps, but combining them with shoulder movement turns them into a delt exercise; never fully extend in that position
Standing dumbbell curls are excellent and the place every beginner should start
Stick to Arnold and excellent tier exercises; decent ones can spice things up, ignore the rest
